error_type_detail: E5-S4 AC5: GET /api/recommendation does not reliably reflect an advisor override that was already committed and acknowledged (201) moments earlier. The single focus/visibilitychange-triggered refetch Allocation.tsx performs can land inside a reproducible ~150-300ms server-side staleness window and return the pre-override risk_band/allocations; since the component only refetches once per focus event (no retry/poll), the customer's tab is left showing the wrong allocation indefinitely, until another focus event happens to land outside the window.
expected: Two-tab scenario per contract steps: tab 1 (customer, active RiskBandAssignment) renders its allocation; tab 2 (advisor) submits a valid override for the same customer to a different risk band; back in tab 1, without any manual reload/navigation, a refetch is observed (GET /api/recommendation re-issued) and the view updates to the overridden band's allocations, within a reasonable wait (up to 15s per the evaluator's instructions).
actual: Reproduced live 3 times with real two-Chromium-context Playwright sessions (Playwright 1.63.0) against the live backend/frontend (localhost:8000/5173), and independently confirmed with 2 direct-HTTP polling scripts bypassing the browser entirely (fetch-based, node 24.18.0): in every run, an override POST resolves 201 and its own response body already carries the new risk_band, but a GET /api/recommendation issued immediately afterward (0ms observed delay in the polling scripts, and the single real focus-triggered fetch in the two-tab browser runs) still returns the PRE-override risk_band. Direct polling isolates the exact window: poll #0 at +0ms after the 201 returns the stale band every time; poll #1 at +150-313ms returns the correct band. In the two browser-context runs (customer bob.nakamura, customer_id=2; advisor overriding CONSERVATIVE->MODERATE then MODERATE->AGGRESSIVE across two separate runs), Allocation.tsx's one-shot focus-triggered refetch landed inside that window both times: the DOM's `dl.meta dd` (risk_band display) never updated to the target band even after polling it for the full 15s wait, because no second refetch is ever triggered - the write was real and eventually visible (confirmed via a follow-up direct API read), but the UI had already consumed its one refetch opportunity on the stale response and had no mechanism to try again.
stack_trace: No exception is raised anywhere - this is a data-consistency race, not a crash. Empirical evidence (5 independent reproductions) is in the 'actual' field above; the request/response pair itself is: POST http://localhost:8000/api/advisor/customers/{id}/override -> 201 (containing the new risk_band), immediately followed by GET http://localhost:8000/api/recommendation -> 200 with the OLD risk_band in the body.

error_type_detail: E9-S4 AC4: CustomerDetail.tsx's post-override refetch (onOverridden -> loadDetail, a single GET /api/advisor/customers/{id} call, no retry) can land inside the same backend read-after-write staleness window documented in pw-h-05, leaving the drill-in view showing the pre-override risk_band and override_history with no new entry, indefinitely (no automatic recovery short of a manual page reload).
expected: Submitting a valid override (new_band=MODERATE, reason supplied) for customer_id=1 (alice.reyes, holdings+goals+active allocation fixture substituted for the contract's illustrative 'customer 3' per the team-lead's guidance) resolves POST .../override 201, then the drill-in view's displayed risk_band updates to MODERATE via state (no navigation/full-page reload), and the override_history list includes the new entry - within a reasonable wait.
actual: Reproduced live with a real Chromium session against the live backend/frontend: override POST resolved 201 in 47ms. Polled the page every ~315ms for 9+ seconds (30 iterations) immediately afterward: `[data-testid=customer-risk-band]` and `[data-testid=override-history]` both remained frozen at their PRE-override values (band still showing the old band; override_history still showing only the prior entry, missing the just-created one) for the entire poll window - the UI never updated. A direct, separate API read moments later (after the script exited) confirmed the write itself was correct and fully committed: `GET /api/advisor/customers/1` returned the new override_history entry with the correct previous_band/new_band. This is the same class of bug as pw-h-05 (see that check's evidence for two isolated HTTP-only repros of the underlying ~150-300ms staleness window), manifesting here because CustomerDetail's `loadDetail()` (triggered once by `onOverridden`) is likewise a one-shot, non-retrying refetch.
